primary.thesis: The ladder itself shows where the price was. The mid-month contracts were added as 'reach $65,000' (C20) and 'dip to $62,500 / $60,000' (C9, C10), and they only count price action after they were created. That places BTC/USDT at roughly $62.5k-65k around 2026-07-16. With about two weeks left in July, reaching the far strikes would take a move of about 15-60% up, or about 15-20% or more down. That is a regime-change move, not normal two-week drift. My thesis is that BTC trades in a broad range of roughly $55k-72k until month-end and the far tails of the ladder expire untouched. The basket sells those tails: two strikes well above the price and two well below it.

basket.reason: $100k is about 55-60% above the implied spot. No two-week catalyst in the documents points to that.
$77.5k needs a sustained rally of about 20%. Price already had to fall into the low $60ks for the $62.5k and $60k dip contracts to be listed, so momentum is not running up.
$52.5k needs about an 18% drop in two weeks. That takes a liquidation cascade or a macro shock, not ordinary chop.
$47.5k is about 25% below spot. It needs a crash on the scale of a crisis within the remaining window.

failure_narrative: The basket loses if realised volatility breaks out of the range in the second half of July. The more likely path is down. The market was already sagging enough to need new dip strikes. A risk-off macro shock, heavy spot-ETF outflows, or a forced seller such as a corporate treasury holder, a miner, an exchange or a government wallet could set off a cascade of leveraged-long liquidations on Binance perps. That would push a one-minute wick through $52.5k and possibly $47.5k. A 1m wick is enough to settle the contract, even if price recovers within minutes. The less likely path is a short squeeze or a policy or ETF-flow headline that rips BTC past $77.5k. Either way, the loss comes from a volatility expansion that tail-sellers did not expect.
hedge_thesis: The worlds where BTC breaks its range, mainly downward, are broad risk-off or deleveraging worlds. In those worlds equity volatility spikes, with the VIX up and the Nasdaq and high-beta tech down. Crypto-linked equities such as Strategy (MicroStrategy), Coinbase and the miners fall even harder, because they are leveraged proxies for BTC and share the same margin and liquidity channels. Money tends to flow into gold and Treasuries as havens. Other large crypto assets like ether wick down together, because cross-margined positions get liquidated at the same time. So instruments that pay out on higher equity volatility, lower tech or crypto-equity prices, or a gold rally tend to win in exactly the worlds where selling the BTC tails loses.
